This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Hanumantharayappa A. caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 18102021 at about 4 p.m.
Hanumantharayappa was riding the passion pro two wheeler bearing reg.No.KA03 HM6803 in to order to go to his residential house at T.C.Palya, Bengaluru from Bandarahalli village, at that time, driver of the Maruti Swift D'zire car bearing No.KA24MA 7684 came with high speed on SH 9 road and hit the deceased from back near Bandrahalli village with high speed, reckless, rash and negligent manner, endangering human life without observing traffic rules and regulations.
Due to impact, Hanumantharayappa fell down and sustained injuries and shifted to Gowribidanur hospital, wherein Hanumantharayappa succumbed to the injuries.

It is further stated that petitioners spent huge amount towards medical, funeral, obsequies expenses and for transportation of deadbody etc., and prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 65 years at the time of death and was retired Assistant police sub Inspector at CAR Head quarters and getting pension of Rs.40,000/p.m. and deceased was owning agricultural land at Bandarahalli village and getting Rs.10 lakhs from agricultural land and was contributing entire earnings to his family.

Due to sudden death of deceased, petitioners are undergoing deep mental shock, mental Uma.H vs Suresha on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125058047/
2 agony and untold hardship.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.50 lakhs from the respondent.
3. After service of notice to respondent, the respondent appeared before this Tribunal and filed written statement.
The respondent in its written statement contended the entire petition averments.

Further contended that accident is caused only due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased by his motor cycle and dashed against the car and compensation claimed by the petitioners are highly exorbitant and fashionable and are not entitled for any compensation.
Hence prays to dismiss the claim petition with exemplary costs.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Hanumantharayappa A S/o Late.Anjinappa sustained grievous injury in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Maruthi Shift car bearing No.KA25MA7684 on 18 102021 at about 4.00 p.m. near Bandarlahalli village, SH9 road,
Gowribidanur Taluk, Chickballapura, he succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the petitioner prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What order or award ?
5. The Petitioner No.4 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked ExP1 to 15 documents on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondent has not lead either oral or documentary evidence.
6. Arguments were addressed on both side.
7. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows : Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Swift D'zire car bearing reg.No.KA 24MA7684, the petitioner No.4 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 13 documents as ExP1 to 13 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizure Uma.H vs Suresha on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125058047/
3 mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report, charge sheet and aadhaar card.
9. The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Gangadharappa S/o Ramalingappa lodged complaint before the Manchenalli PS as per ExP2.
Based on the complaint, Manchenalli police registered FIR as per ExP1.

On the basis of the complaint, jurisdictional police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet as per ExP7 by holding that on 181 2021 at about 4.00p.m. when deceased Hanumantharayappa was riding the motor cycle bearing No.KA03HM6803 from Bandarahalli village towards Bangalore on the left side of the road, at that time, accused by name Dinesh Yadav who was driving the offending vehicle Maruti swift D'zire car bearing reg.No.KA24MA7684 belonging to accused No.2/respondent No.1 drove the car in high speed, rash and negligent manner in the same direction behind the motor cycle of the deceased Hanumantharayappa and hit to the hind portion of the motor cycle of the deceased Hanumantharayappa near Chikkaballapura in front of the field of Veerathippaiah and thereby caused accident.
Due to impact, Hanumantharayappa fell down and sustained injuries and he was taken to the nearby hospital where he declared as dead.

The IO has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the Maruti swift car bearing No.KA24MA7684 for the offence punishable u/s 279, 304 A of IPC and filed the charge sheet against the respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle u/s 146, 196 of IMV Ac for not having the valid insurance to the vehicle and allowed the vehicle to be run on the public road.
10. Though learned counsel for the respondent cross examined PW1 at length, but nothing was elicited from his mouth.
PW1 has outrightly denied the suggestions made by the respondent counsel with regard to the rash and negligent riding of the deceased.

11. Though counsel for the respondent has disputed the rash and negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle but has not examined the driver of the offending vehicle to prove his contention or disprove the evidence of PW1.
The driver of the Maruti swift car being one of the eye witness and material witness has not been examined by the respondent No.1 to prove his contention.
Even there are no materials to prove that the charge sheet is defective and collusive.

12. Apart from this, on perusal of exP3 spot mahazar and ExP5 sketch, it clearly shows that spot of accident is a state highway road with two way and accident had been taken place on the extreme left edge of the road from Bandarahalli towards Bangalore.
ExP5 clearly shows that the accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Moreover respondent has not at all challenging and disputed the ExP3 and ExP5.
Moreover respondent has not examined the driver of the car who is the material witness to state as to why he has drove his car towards extreme left side and thereby caused accident and non Uma.
H vs Suresha

on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125058047/
4 examination of the driver of the car is a material.
Moreover respondent has not disputed the documents placed on the record by the petitioner and particularly ExP5 and the charge sheet.
There are absolutely no materials placed on record to prove that the charge sheet is collusive and defective.
All these documents clearly shows that the car was involved in the accident.
Moreover all these documents have not at all been disputed by the respondents.

13. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari vs Amir Chand & Ors  wherein it has been held that  "In a situation of this nature,
the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.

entities.text: AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari vs Amir Chand & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
14. Thus, the oral evidence of PW1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
15. Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA24MA7684.
16.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

entities.text: MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
17. ISSUES NO.2 :
The petitioner No.4 filed affidavit in lieu of his chiefexamination and deposed that he is the son, petitioners No.1 to 3 are his sisters and petitioner No.5 is his mother.
The documents which are exhibited at Ex's.P8 to 13 i.e., adhaar cards reflect that the petitioner No.1 to 4 are daughters, son and petitioner No.5 is the wife of deceased Hanumantharayappa.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents, as is evident from the tenor of cross examination of PW.1.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
PW1 in the cross examination admitted that petitioner No.1 to 3 are his elder sisters and married and residing in their matrimonial house.
In this regard on perusal of the cause title of the petition it reveals that petitioner No.1 to 3 are the married and major and are residing in their matrimonial houses.

Hence,
it is clear that petitioner No.1 to 3 are not dependent on the deceased.
Hence, petitioner No.1 to 3 are only entitled for the compensation under the conservative heads.
Hence issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.
18. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:

From ExP13 Aadhaar card, it reveals that Hanumantharayappa date of birth is 1956 and as on the date of accident,

5

entities.text: Uma.H vs Suresha on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hanumantharayappa was aged 65 years.

Admittedly the deceased was married and the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group of 61 to 65 is '7'.
19.
As admitted by the PW1 that deceased was retired Police SubInspector.
Further himself admitted that as of now his mother was getting family pension.

Further though petitioner has not produced any documents to show how much pension his mother was getting but later on petitioner produced the family pension slip of his mother as per ExP14 and pension slip of his father as Ex P15.
As per ExP15 as on the date of death of Hanumantharayapa was getting pension of Rs.20,529/ p.m. and as per ExP14 his mother is getting pension of Rs.19,624/p.m.

Even PW1 in the cross examination clearly admitted that his father was getting the pension of rs.20,529/
p.m. at the time of his death and even his mother has also getting family pension.

Though petitioner contended that his father was getting Rs.40,000/p.m. but as per ExP15 his father a getting the pension of Rs.20,529/ p.m. and even as per ExP14 now also mother mother of the petitioners i.e.,
wife of the deceased

was getting family pension of Rs.19,624/. Hence there is only loss of Rs.900/
p.m. due to death of Hanumantharayappa.
20. The deceased was married and having two dependents.
Hence 1/3rd of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/3rd of Rs.900/ works out to Rs.300/.
Income for consideration is Rs.600/ (900 - 300).
Annual income works out to Rs.7,200/ (600 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '7'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.50,400/ (7200 X 7).
21. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Petitioner No.1 to 5 being daughters,
son and wife of the deceased are entitled to the consortium of Rs.48,400/ each.
22. LOSS OF ESTATE:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
23. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

24. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : Rs.50,40000 2 Loss of Consortium : Rs.2,42,00000 3 Loss of Estate : Rs.18,15000 4 Funeral Expenses : Rs.18,15000 Total Rs.3,28,700=00

Hence, petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.3,28,700=00.
25.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it Uma.H vs Suresha on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125058047/
6 would meet the ends of justice.

26. Therefore, the respondent being the RC owner is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent being the owner of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
27. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER :
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners No.4 and 5

are entitled for the compensation of Rs.86,700/
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The petitioners No.1 to 5 are equally entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,42,000/ (consortium) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit together with interest, out of the compensation amount Rs.86,700/ the petitioner No.4 & 5 are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows:
 Petitioner No.4 30  %
 Petitioner No.5 70  %
Out of the compensation amount
, entire share awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 5 shall be released to them through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
(Dictated to stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 13th day of September 2024).
